coverageNote: CMMC Level 2: all 110 security requirements of NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2, which 32 CFR 170.14(c)(2) states "are identical to the requirements in NIST SP 800-171 R2." What is solid here, stated plainly: (1) Every topicSummary is the VERBATIM requirement text from NIST SP 800-171 R2, extracted from the NIST-hosted PDF at nvlpubs.nist.gov. NIST states in that document that it "is not subject to copyright in the United States," so unlike the HITRUST, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 modules this one ships the authoritative wording rather than a paraphrase. Attribution to NIST is requested by NIST and is carried in every citation. (2) The enumeration is 110 requirements across 14 families (3.1 Access Control 22, 3.2 Awareness and Training 3, 3.3 Audit and Accountability 9, 3.4 Configuration Management 9, 3.5 Identification and Authentication 11, 3.6 Incident Response 3, 3.7 Maintenance 6, 3.8 Media Protection 9, 3.9 Personnel Security 2, 3.10 Physical Protection 6, 3.11 Risk Assessment 3, 3.12 Security Assessment 4, 3.13 System and Communications Protection 16, 3.14 System and Information Integrity 7). It was cross-checked against the document's own Appendix D mapping tables -- an independently typeset listing of the same identifiers elsewhere in the publication -- and the two sets matched exactly, 110 of 110, with no id in one and not the other. Three extraction traps are recorded because each would have shipped confident wrong output: the running footer merges into some requirement lines and silently swallowed 3.1.5; a 1..n sequentiality check cannot detect a missing LAST child, so it is not sufficient on its own; and pdftotext -layout collapses the multi-column requirement pages, scrambling 3.1.6 through 3.1.8 -- -simple mode is what pairs ids with their statements correctly. (3) Every topicLabel is DERIVED, cut from the requirement's own opening clause. Revision 2 gives no per-requirement titles (Revision 3 does), so these are ours: readable, but carrying no authority. Read the topicSummary for the requirement itself. (4) IMPORTANT VERSION TRAP: NIST WITHDREW SP 800-171 R2 on 14 May 2024 and superseded it with Revision 3. CMMC still binds Revision 2 -- 32 CFR 170.2 incorporates it by reference, and the rule was not updated to R3. An organization that assesses itself against the current NIST publication is assessing against the wrong control set for CMMC purposes. This module deliberately tracks the withdrawn R2 because that is what the regulation requires. (5) Level 2 applies to CUI and is validated either by a C3PAO certification assessment or, for a subset of programs, by self-assessment -- which one applies is set by your contract, not by this tool. Confirm scope, level and assessment type with your contracting officer and your C3PAO.
